claims.originalText: Classic Chinese furniture is an art of carpentry and joinery, which makes use of a mortise-and-tenon framework.

qualifiers.attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art; captured record, not independent authentication
qualifiers.editorialScope: Object-specific or explicitly bounded comparison; no certificate implied

variants.text: Classic Chinese furniture is an art of carpentry and joinery, which makes use of a mortise-and-tenon framework.
中國古典家具結合木作與接合工藝，使用榫卯框架。

claims.originalText: The back of the chair is made of seven pieces of wood, joined and secured with an inserted wooden pin, a mortise-tenon technique that appeared in its earliest form in Neolitihic fragments of the Hemudu culture.

qualifiers.attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art; captured record, not independent authentication
qualifiers.editorialScope: Object-specific or explicitly bounded comparison; no certificate implied

variants.text: The back of the chair is made of seven pieces of wood, joined and secured with an inserted wooden pin, a mortise-tenon technique that appeared in its earliest form in Neolitihic fragments of the Hemudu culture.

claims.originalText: The horseshoe-shaped back of this chair is joined without glue or nails.
